result:
The UI already gates both buttons on `canManage`; the gap was purely server-side.

`PostController.destroy()` fetched the post and deleted it without ever consulting the gate, so any authenticated session could delete any post. I added `await this.authorize('delete', [Post, post])` immediately after the `findOrFail(id)` in `app/Http/Controllers/PostController.ts:99-107`, mirroring exactly what `edit()`/`update()` already do — the `PostPolicy.delete()` rule (`user !== null && Number(user.id) === post.authorId`) and its registration in `AuthorizationProvider` were already in place, so no policy change was needed; a non-author now gets a 403 from the thrown `AuthorizationException`, guests are still stopped by the `auth` middleware on the route group, and the author's own delete is unaffected. I also extended `tests/PostController.test.ts` with a `posts.destroy` suite covering all three cases (author deletes successfully and the row is gone; a signed-in stranger gets 403 with the post still present; a guest is refused). `bun run typecheck` passes and `bun test` reports 5 pass / 0 fail.
